message.content:
A CPU (Central Processing Unit) and a GPU (Graphics Processing Unit) are both processors, but they’re designed for different kinds of workloads:

| Feature | CPU | GPU |
|---------|-----|-----|
| **Purpose** | General‑purpose computing – handles everything from OS tasks to application logic. | Specialized for highly parallel tasks – originally for rendering graphics, now also used for scientific, machine‑learning, and other compute‑intensive workloads. |
| **Architecture** | Few cores (typically 2–32), each core is powerful, with deep pipelines, sophisticated branch prediction, large caches, and complex control logic. | Hundreds or thousands of lightweight cores arranged in SIMD (Single Instruction, Multiple Data) groups; each core is simpler but many can work simultaneously on the same instruction stream. |
| **Instruction Set** | Complex instruction set (CISC) or reduced instruction set (RISC) with many features (branch prediction, out‑of‑order execution). | Mostly simple, fixed‑function pipelines optimized for throughput; less emphasis on latency. |
| **Memory Hierarchy** | Large L1/L2/L3 caches per core, high bandwidth memory interface, support for virtual memory and paging. | Smaller per‑core caches, rely heavily on high‑bandwidth shared memory (VRAM) and specialized cache hierarchies (texture caches, constant caches). |
| **Latency vs Throughput** | Optimized for low latency – quick response to single-threaded or few‑threaded workloads. | Optimized for high throughput – can process millions of data elements in parallel, even if each element takes longer. |
| **Typical Workloads** | Single‑threaded or lightly parallel tasks: OS kernel, web browsers, office apps, database queries. | Data‑parallel tasks: image/video processing, physics simulations, deep learning inference/training, cryptocurrency mining. |
| **Programming Model** | Traditional imperative programming (C/C++, Java, etc.) with thread libraries (pthreads, OpenMP). | Parallel programming models (CUDA, OpenCL, Vulkan compute, DirectCompute, Metal, etc.) that expose massive SIMD execution. |
| **Power Efficiency** | Power‑efficient for general tasks, but each core consumes more power due to complex logic. | Very power‑efficient per FLOP because of simpler cores and higher clock rates; overall power consumption can be high when fully utilized. |

### Key Takeaways

* **CPU** = “brain” for general-purpose tasks, excels at branching, complex logic, and low‑latency operations.
* **GPU** = “muscle” for massively parallel, data‑centric tasks, excels at throughput and handling many identical operations simultaneously.

In modern systems, CPUs and GPUs often cooperate: the CPU orchestrates tasks and handles serial parts, while the GPU accelerates the heavy, parallel portions. This synergy is why GPUs have become popular beyond graphics—for AI training, scientific computing, and real‑time analytics.
